title: Why look beyond positive and negative reviews?
source: Nikitina & Furuoka (2023); Nandwani & Verma (2021).
text: Why look beyond positive and negative reviews?
Perfume reviews describe sensory impressions and emotional associations.
Two positive reviews; different emotional meanings. Illustrative examples.
Emotion classification offers a more detailed description of review language.

title: One review can express several emotions
text: One review can express several emotions
“This perfume makes me happy, and I cannot wait to wear it.”
The task allows multiple emotion labels for the same perfume, based on its review text.
Target: emotion expressed in review language. Wearer responses are not directly measured.

title: How certain is the effect of augmentation?
source: Thesis §4.4.3; Table 11. Seven-label Macro AP; 95% paired source-group intervals. Exact values: A4.
text: FROM OBSERVED CHANGES TO SUPPORTED CONCLUSIONS
How certain is the effect of augmentation?
Thesis §4.4.3; Table 11. Seven-label Macro AP; 95% paired source-group intervals. Exact values: A4.

Change = augmented Macro AP − natural-only Macro AP.
Positive means improvement; negative means decline.
Recalculate the difference for many samples of source groups, each given equal weight.
For all five models, the range includes both negative and positive AP changes.
Zero means no change. Ranges crossing zero leave the direction uncertain.
The observed gains need further confirmation; augmentation should be validated for each model.

title: What the experiments establish together
source: Thesis §§6.2–6.3. Observed differences are interpreted within the tested configurations.
text: Thesis §§6.2–6.3. Observed differences are interpreted within the tested configurations.
58 features organise word associations, affect and contextual scores into shared inputs for three classifiers.
BERT leads F1 and AP; the 58-feature XGBoost route leads ROC-AUC. Label decisions and score rankings measure different aspects.
More training text must be tested on natural reviews
With the same natural test data, augmentation raises Logistic Regression’s AP and lowers BERT’s. A general gain is not established.

title: Three takeaways
text: 58 named features connect lexical, affective and contextual information.
A clear comparison of two input routes

A measured test of additional training data
